learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the connection and mutual dependence of vehicles, infrastructure, and operation in a railway system.
They derive requirements for a high-performance infrastructure and suitable rail vehicle concepts from operational specifications and legal frameworks.
They recognize the influence of alignment, understand the system-defining function of wheel-rail contact, and estimate the effects of driving dynamics on the operating program.
They assess the effects of operating procedures on the safety and performance of the railway system.
They learn about the infrastructure for energy supply to rail vehicles of different traction types.
Students recognize the tasks of rail vehicles and understand their classification.
They understand their basic structure and learn the functions of the main systems. They recognize the overarching tasks of vehicle system technology.
They learn the functions and requirements of the car body and assess the advantages and disadvantages of different construction methods.
They understand the functionalities of the car body's external interfaces.
They understand the basics of running gear technology and its implementation in bogies.
They learn the advantages and disadvantages of different drive types and decide which is best suited for which application.
They understand braking technology with its vehicle-side and operational aspects and assess the suitability of different braking systems.
They learn the basic structure of control technology and understand the functions of the most important components.
Based on the requirements for modern rail vehicles, they specify and define suitable vehicle concepts.
Depending on the choice of elective subjects, students learn further important aspects of a railway system.

syllabus_topics: The Railway System: Railway as a system, subsystems and interactions, definitions, laws, regulations, rail and environment, economic importance of the railway
Operation: Transport tasks, public local transport, regional transport, long-distance transport, freight transport, operational planning

Infrastructure: Railway and operational facilities, alignment elements (track curves, superelevation, clothoid, longitudinal gradient), stations (platform lengths, platform heights), clearance gauge and vehicle limitation
Wheel-rail contact: Carrying vehicle weight, transmitting traction and braking forces, guiding the wheelset in the track, returning current in electric traction vehicles
Driving dynamics: Traction and braking force, running resistance force, inertia force, typical driving cycles (local, long-distance traffic)
Operations management: Elements of operations management, train protection, train separation control, train control, European Train Control System, blocked time, automatic driving

Railway energy supply: Energy supply for rail vehicles, comparison of electric traction / diesel traction, railway power grids (DC, AC with special frequency, AC with national frequency), pantograph-catenary system, energy supply for diesel traction vehicles
System structure of rail vehicles: Tasks and classification, main systems, vehicle system engineering
Car body: Functions, requirements, design principles, construction methods, energy-absorbing elements, couplings and transitions, doors and windows

Running gear: Forces on the wheel, wheelset guidance, steering axle running gear, bogie, Jacobs bogie, active running gear components, longitudinal force transmission to the car body, wheelset sequence

Drive: Principle drive types, electric power transmission (main components, asynchronous traction motor, inverter, power supply from DC network, power supply from AC network, no network supply, multi-system, dual-power and hybrid vehicles), non-electric power transmission

Brakes: Fundamentals, operating principles of brakes (wheel brakes, rail brakes, blending), brake control (requirements and operating modes, compressed air brake, electro-pneumatic brake, emergency brake, parking brake)
Vehicle control technology: Definition of vehicle control technology, bus systems & components, network architectures, examples of controls, future developments
Vehicle concepts: Tram and light rail, metro, suburban rail, regional multiple units, intercity trains, high-speed trains, double-deck vehicles, locomotives, freight wagons
Further content depending on the choice of supplementary subjects
assessment_rules: Oral exams will be approximately 5 minutes per ECTS credit. The number, form, and scope of assessments may vary depending on the individual choice of partial services.
